source.note: "List project merge requests" filtered by its documented `state` ("just those that are opened") and `source_branch` ("Returns merge requests with the given source branch") attributes; the list item is the page's merge request object with this corpus's values for merge request 7 (the same author, branch and head as `merge-requests.json`), and the members the adapter never reads removed. WP-138's adoption read.
The page does not publish the answer for a filter nothing matches; an empty array is inferred from the endpoint being a filtered list. The adapter answers null for it.

"Retrieve the current user" (`GET /user`) example response for a regular user, cut to the members the adapter reads plus `bot`, with this corpus's own bot account (id 4242, the author of every merge request in this corpus).

"Create merge request pipeline" (`POST /projects/:id/merge_requests/:merge_request_iid/pipelines`) — the endpoint and its two attributes were read from the page's search excerpt ("Create a new pipeline for a merge request. A pipeline created via this endpoint doesn't run a regular branch/tag pipeline"); the rendered page did not show the section when fetched, and its example response was not read. The body is the pipeline object of the pipelines page (`id`, `sha`, `ref`, `status`, `source`, `web_url`) with status `created` and the merge-request ref, inferred rather than transcribed.

The status table documents "404 Not Found - A resource couldn't be accessed"; the body for a merge request that does not exist is not published for this endpoint and is the shape the corpus's other 404s use. Only the status is load-bearing.
